en-feb03e76.text: Who provided you food and drink?

en-783b6c61.text: Every morning the sun rises in the east. Every evening it sets in the west. Then the stars come out, and the morning comes again.

en-6956dcba.text: Never early. Never late. Have you ever wondered who keeps it all in order?

en-5cae68c9.text: Who makes the night follow the day, and the day follow the night?

en-fcf0abbd.text: Things begin. They grow. They get better.

en-c93e9bd8.text: Who is behind all of it?

en-d9462b6d.text: Mountains. Storms. Cities. Nothing is too big or too strong to be under His control.

en-9da43053.text: Allah asks these very questions in the Quran. And He tells us how they answer.

en-0daee1e6.text: Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who manages every affair? They will say: Allah. So say: Then will you not be mindful of Him?

en-b3ea0734.text: Who makes the night enter into the day and the day enter into the night, every single day, never late?

en-2c2b5582.text: Allah does. He manages the sky and the earth.

en-bc828a57.text: The sun rises in the east, crosses the sky and sets in the west. Stars come out. The sun rises again.

en-b78e6ac9.text: If nobody were in charge, would it stay so perfectly in order?

en-a246d3c2.text: Who gives life and growth? And when someone is ill and then gets better, who gives the healing?

en-391b133b.text: Allah does. We do our part: we see a doctor, take medicine and rest. Those are the means Allah lets us use, and the cure comes from Him.

en-6004e258.text: A seed becomes a plant. An egg becomes a chick. A wilted flower opens again after the rain.

en-191e52a1.text: Can a doctor or a farmer make life start by themselves?

en-3605785f.text: You make the night enter into the day and You make the day enter into the night, You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account.

en-c4774e21.text: Who is in charge of the strongest, the richest and the most powerful?

en-92a15e8a.text: Allah is. He owns everything. He gives power to whom He wills and takes it away from whom He wills.

en-f80d2166.text: A great mountain. A storm that passes over it. A distant city with its lights coming on.

en-8bc9fffc.text: Is anyone too important to be under Allah’s control?

en-c47a1777.text: Say: O Allah, Owner of all sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take it from whom You will, You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You have power over all things.

en-8d6ce07a.text: In the Quran Allah asks: who provides for you, and who manages every affair? What do people answer?

en-34b27d0c.text: The same dawn we began with, quiet and wide.

en-c85dcf87.text: This ayah shows that provision, ownership, giving life, causing death and managing every affair are all in Allah’s hand alone.

en-f66ea1ca.text: What does it mean when I say رَبِّيَ اللهُ, my Lord is Allah?

en-09cf921b.text: He provides for me and for all creatures.

en-a96191fe.text: He controls and manages every affair.

en-da6da181.text: The One who does all three is the only One who deserves our worship. The next unit begins there.

en-326665b7.text: I woke up before sunrise today. The sky was dark, then grey, then gold, and the sun came up over the east, just like yesterday.

en-3c23fd5e.text: It made me wonder. The sun has done this every morning of my whole life, and every morning of my parents’ lives, and their parents’ lives. It has never been late.

en-c0c16eb2.text: Allah makes the night enter into the day and the day enter into the night.

en-ed0a98f4.text: Last winter I had a fever. My mum took me to the doctor, I took my medicine, and I rested. After a few days I was better.

en-57d2d5a7.text: The doctor helped, and the medicine helped, and I am thankful for both. But I asked myself a question: who gave the healing?

en-67967dd5.text: Allah gives the healing, and we use the means He allows.

en-0cfe05b1.text: Then I thought about everything else. Seeds that turn into trees. Storms that come and go. Leaders who are powerful one year and gone the next. Nobody planned all of that by themselves.

en-f4ade03f.text: So when I say رَبِّيَ اللهُ, my Lord is Allah, I mean three things. He created me and everything. He provides for me and for every living thing. And He controls and manages everything He created.

en-78ee95c9.text: And if Allah is the One who does all of that, then He is the One who deserves my worship.

en-067fb68c.text: Allah provides for me and for all creatures.

en-26d3f1dd.text: Allah controls and manages every affair.

en-d55a5ba5.text: The sun is setting and the first stars are coming out.

en-0fb8dcb8.text: Morning light spreads over the hills as the night ends.

en-8c254280.text: A small green shoot is pushing up out of the soil.

en-2be3626a.text: An egg cracks open and a chick steps out.

en-49feae74.text: A child had a fever. She took her medicine, rested, and now she feels better.

en-f9d7151d.text: Who makes the night follow the day?

en-8d48ba98.text: Allah makes the night follow the day.

en-49646925.text: What are the three things my Lord does?

en-c7ddef4e.text: Four lessons, one idea. Allah created us, Allah provides for us, and Allah manages every affair.

en-83c5e5c4.text: If all of that is true, there is one question left. What do we owe Him?

en-ef0ac4cf.text: Not by accident. He created us for a purpose, and He tells us exactly what it is.

en-ed673846.text: Allah created me to worship Him alone.

en-e684345a.text: Ask most people what worship is and they will say prayer. They are right.

en-36c4de30.text: Prayer is one of the greatest acts of worship, and it belongs to a whole family of them.

en-75c064bb.text: Some worship happens quietly in the heart: loving Allah, hoping in Him, fearing Him, and relying on Him completely.

en-2dad0257.text: Other worship happens through what we say and do.

ar-1c167120.text: الْعِبَادَةُ: كُلُّ مَا يُحِبُّهُ اللهُ مِنَ الْأَقْوَالِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ

en-2c1897f7.text: Worship is everything Allah loves, of words and of actions.

en-1353f9ff.text: So why worship Him? Not from fear alone. From love.

en-ee1d6923.text: He created us, He provided for us, and He made us Muslims.

ar-acfa6cf0.text: أُحِبُّ اللهَ وَأُطِيعُهُ لِأَنَّهُ خَلَقَنِي وَرَزَقَنِي وَلِأَنَّهُ جَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ

en-8d868245.text: I love Allah and I obey Him, because He created me, provided for me, and made me one of the Muslims.

en-3151054a.text: And because He alone does all of this, worship belongs to Him alone. The Quran says it plainly.

en-be06de86.text: I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.

en-d7215133.text: The One who creates, provides and manages every affair is the only One who deserves worship.

en-191a8ce8.text: Finish this sentence in your own words: “Allah alone deserves my worship because…”

ar-f1f1790c.text: يَجِبُ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَدْعُوَ اللهَ وَلَا أَدْعُوَ مَعَهُ غَيْرَهُ

en-e31cbc50.text: I must call on Allah, and never call on anyone else together with Him.

en-22effd4f.text: Allah is the One who provides and manages every affair, so He is the One to ask for what only He can give. Asking anyone else for that would treat them as if they were in charge of it.

en-6a02da92.text: It is completely fine to ask people for help with things they are able to do, like a friend for a pencil or a parent for a lift. What we ask Allah alone for is what only He can give, such as good health, guidance and forgiveness.

en-ad5472e5.text: Asking a friend for a pencil and asking Allah for good health are both asking. Why are they different?

en-01079ba8.text: Asking Allah, aloud or silently, for anything at all, big or small.

en-4ae3e35e.text: Three gifts sit behind that sentence. He created me, He provided for me, and He made me one of the Muslims. Love makes obedience feel like thanks rather than a chore.

en-3ebac4b1.text: A Muslim also stays mindful of Allah.

en-caa52169.text: A Muslim fears Allah and does not disobey Him.

en-cbe9ad9b.text: This fear is respect and awe, and it sits alongside love. Together they keep us from disobeying Him.

ar-0248f19e.text: أَنَا أُصَلِّي لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ اللهَ وَأُطِيعُهُ

en-e215c5c6.text: I pray because I love Allah and obey Him.

en-347bf25d.text: Say the same sentence about a different act of worship.

en-ca3e65c8.text: Some worship is quiet and inward, like loving Allah, hoping in Him, fearing to disobey Him, and relying on Him completely. This is worship of the heart.

en-10d37130.text: Some worship is said or done, like prayer, fasting, honesty and charity. This is worship of the tongue and the limbs. Prayer is one of the greatest acts of this kind, and it stays at the centre of a Muslim’s day.

en-829d4954.text: Notice how many of these happen outside the mosque. Honesty at school and kindness to a neighbour are worship when they are done for Allah’s sake and in the way He loves.

en-dd077c9d.text: Truthfulness is loved. Disobeying parents and harming a neighbour are disliked.

en-0999ffc9.text: Think of one word you said today and one action you did that Allah loves.

en-2f40c901.text: Doing my part and trusting Allah with the result is worship.

en-d2cf6943.text: In Level 4 we learned that Allah manages every affair. That is why tawakkul makes sense.

en-fbef2e1f.text: Studying for a test is your part. Trusting Allah with the result is tawakkul.

en-9593b45c.text: Dua and tawakkul work together: you ask Him, you do your part, and you trust Him.

en-49280294.text: You have a hard test tomorrow. Which part is yours, and which part do you trust Allah with?

I read a page of the Quran. I put a coin in the charity box. And when I felt nervous about my spelling test, I asked Allah for help.

en-a7389ac6.text: Then I remembered what we had learned.

en-0fa24092.text: Saying salaam is a word. Carrying shopping is an action. Telling the truth is both. None of them happened in a mosque, and every one of them counted.

en-d99288ea.text: A classmate once asked me, Why do you bother with all that? I could have said, Because I have to. But the honest answer is bigger.

en-ca964ea6.text: The spelling test taught me something too. I asked Allah for help, and I also studied.

en-dc1f6235.text: Asking Him is called dua. Doing my part and then trusting Him with the result is called tawakkul.

en-a9556492.text: When I add it all up, my whole day belongs to Him: my words, my actions, my asking and my trusting. That is what I mean when I say that only Allah deserves my worship.

en-56d12bfe.text: I love Allah and I obey Him.

en-586a529f.text: Greeting first with salaam is a word Allah loves, and it spreads peace between people.

en-0008d079.text: Relying on Allah while doing your part.

en-8343d1e8.text: Reading the Quran means saying the words Allah sent down, and every letter read brings a reward.

en-d16e2a3b.text: Making dua is asking Allah, and asking Him shows we know that He alone can give.

en-1dc81227.text: Going to the mosque to pray is an action Allah loves, and every step toward it is rewarded.

en-bcb7abda.text: Giving charity is an action Allah loves, and it helps people in need.

en-6f19bbdd.text: Visiting relatives keeps family ties strong, which Allah commands.

en-dd5c8e0b.text: Telling the truth even when it is uncomfortable

en-e17eeac2.text: We believe that Allah alone is Lord and alone deserves worship.

en-1e86a1db.text: And we reject shirk, which is giving anyone a share in what belongs to Allah alone.

en-d5b03a35.text: The Prophet ﷺ described Islam as a building. It stands on five pillars.

en-f075f486.text: Islam is to submit to Allah by tawhid, to yield to Him by obeying Him, and to disown shirk and its people.

en-58972d7a.text: The testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah.

en-b463e0ba.text: A building stands on its pillars, and it leans if one is missing. Each pillar holds up a different part of a Muslim’s life.

en-391c00af.text: The testimony is the doorway into Islam. Prayer is our daily connection with Allah. Zakat is sharing part of our wealth with people in need.

en-ef9bc71d.text: Fasting in Ramadan trains self control and mindfulness of Allah. Hajj is the pilgrimage to His House in Makkah, for those who are able.

en-cbca33f8.text: Say the five pillars in the order the hadith gives them.

en-5f133e92.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Islam is built on five: the testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj to the House.

en-88e4a856.text: The first pillar has two halves.

en-77a5f56e.text: That there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

en-1bd39c7a.text: That is everything Levels 1 to 5 taught: He alone creates, provides, manages every affair, and deserves worship.

en-eae5475b.text: And that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah.

en-d78f5c7b.text: Holding this belief with confidence does not mean being unkind. Islam also asks for honesty, fairness and kindness toward everyone we meet, including classmates and neighbours of other faiths.

en-acf5a80d.text: That is the next level, where we meet him.

en-a3c550ee.text: On Monday a new girl called Maria joined Aisha’s class. At break she asked, What exactly is Islam? It was a big question for a Monday morning, so Aisha took a breath and answered it in parts.

en-c71f749d.text: Islam means submitting to Allah: believing that He alone is Lord and alone deserves worship, obeying Him, and staying clear of shirk.

en-adaa27b8.text: Maria asked what Muslims actually do. Aisha explained that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught that

en-20654438.text: Islam is built on five pillars, like a house.

en-9fdd64a2.text: The testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan, and Hajj.

en-de6db4ff.text: Maria said she believed something different. They still sat together at lunch and talked about their favourite books. Nothing about their friendship changed.

en-a4b294dc.text: That evening Aisha thought about how easy it would be to feel unsure with so many opinions around her. So she said the dua from her lesson.

en-f4cb1861.text: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ

en-7579061e.text: Five times every day a Muslim stops to pray, starting before sunrise with Fajr.

en-37c502f9.text: In Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn to sunset and break the fast in the evening.

en-52d83e6b.text: Once a year, a Muslim who has enough wealth gives a set part of it to people in need.

en-1b4a966b.text: Every year, pilgrims from around the world come to the Kaaba in Makkah for Hajj.

en-dbd27d83.text: In Level 4 we learned that Allah manages every affair, and that includes hearts.

en-ffcb2ee9.text: In the first levels we learned that Allah created us, provides for us, and manages every affair. And He did not create us and then leave us alone.

en-101dc6a2.text: Allah gave us a purpose: to worship Him alone. And He did not leave us to work out how. He sent us messengers, and a way of life to follow.

en-12ac85c2.text: Different times, different places, different peoples. But one message. Every one of them called people to worship Allah alone, and to submit to Him.

en-a84b460d.text: Allah created us for a purpose, and He did not leave us without guidance. He sent messengers and gave us a way of life to follow.

en-50908cff.text: Level 5 taught that we were created to worship Allah alone. A purpose with no guidance would leave people guessing, and Allah, in His mercy, did not leave us guessing. He sent messenger after messenger to show us how.

en-2aa262ef.text: Name two messengers. What did every one of them call people to?

en-704a5017.text: someone Allah chose to deliver His message to people.

en-94b32601.text: freely accepting Allah as Lord and following what He asks.

en-c7b46046.text: Then Maria asked something harder. Do you think your religion is the right one? Aisha’s heart beat a little faster. She told the truth, because honesty is part of her religion too.

en-75c1ad72.text: She believes that Islam is the religion Allah accepts, and she holds to it with confidence.

en-28b1bbea.text: Then she shared something she had just learned in her lesson.

en-5b326301.text: She said it gently, and added, because kindness is also part of her religion, that she would treat Maria fairly and kindly whatever she believed.

en-eef6bdaa.text: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. That is the first half of what a Muslim declares. There is a second half.

en-29ee3f99.text: Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah.

en-656a06a7.text: Nobody worked this out alone. Someone taught it to us.

en-f1925403.text: Who taught us the religion of Islam?

en-d702ab1c.text: He was not sent to one town, or one people. He was sent to everyone.

en-e6563a45.text: Allah sent him to all people.

en-cf4f6b48.text: And what he asked of every one of them was the same thing we have been learning since Level 1.

en-c716a70b.text: To call them to worship Allah alone and to leave the worship of anyone else.

en-228db01f.text: Our Prophet is Muhammad ﷺ, son of Abdullah, son of Abdul Muttalib.

en-e9b20f87.text: Islam did not appear out of nowhere in our lives. Someone taught it, and that person was a real man, from a real family, at a real time.

en-a4be3735.text: Say his full name, son of Abdullah, son of Abdul Muttalib, and finish it with ﷺ.

en-9ac3f49b.text: Allah sent him to all people, everywhere.

en-fe88a4fc.text: Earlier prophets were sent to their own communities. He was sent to everyone, in every place, for the rest of time. That includes you.

en-b7e0837c.text: To call them to worship Allah alone and to leave the worship of anyone else. This is the same call every prophet came with, back to Level 5.

en-db904fde.text: In one sentence, what was he sent to tell people?

en-a455f089.text: He did not choose his own teachings. He passed on what Allah revealed to him, so obeying him means obeying Allah.

en-76b3bde9.text: This matters. He was a man, not divine, not to be worshipped or prayed to. He himself asked to be described as a slave of Allah and His Messenger, in that order, so we never place him where only Allah belongs.

en-bd2fa446.text: Being a slave of Allah does not make him ordinary. He is still the best of mankind, still loved, still obeyed, still ﷺ after his name every time.

en-717a30b2.text: One evening Aisha’s grandmother asked her, Who taught you everything you know about Allah and Islam?

en-75445d5f.text: Aisha thought about it properly before answering. She had learned it from her mum, and her teacher, and this app. But none of them made it up.

en-efb1df75.text: Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, son of Abdullah, son of Abdul Muttalib,

en-7b8f4274.text: is the one who first taught it, and everyone since has been passing it on.

en-879b76f0.text: And why should that matter to me, her grandmother asked, here, so far from where he lived? Aisha smiled, because she knew this one.

en-d29b187e.text: Allah sent him to all people, everywhere, not only to the people of his own town.

en-b981c6d9.text: Her grandmother asked one more question, a harder one. Do Muslims worship him, then? Aisha shook her head firmly.

en-11aa3d10.text: He is loved, and obeyed, and the best of mankind, but worship belongs to Allah alone.

en-08e9bbb4.text: Aisha’s grandmother nodded slowly. That is a careful answer, she said. Keep learning it that carefully.

en-7baddab4.text: That night, before Aisha slept, she said what her lesson had taught her, three times, the way she does every morning and evening.

en-d7235f9e.text: Allah sent messengers to every people, among them Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus), and the last of them, Muhammad ﷺ. Peace be upon them all. Each one called people to the same thing: to worship Allah alone and to submit to Him. The details of their laws differed, but submission to Allah alone was the religion of every one of them. That submission has a name, and the next panel gives it.

en-03a6f9fa.text: Levels 1 to 5 taught that Allah alone is Lord and alone deserves worship. So a Muslim submits to Him alone, obeys Him, and stays clear of shirk. This is the same submission every messenger practised, from Nuh to Muhammad ﷺ.
